findings.title: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` passes an unsupported kwarg to `self.paginate` and uses a non-datetime paginator on `-datetime`
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` calls `self.paginate(..., paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, order_by="-datetime", ..., enable_advanced_features=True)`. First, `Endpoint.paginate` does not accept `enable_advanced_features` and does not forward `**kwargs` to `paginator_cls`, so any request with `optimized_pagination=true` from a superuser or global-access member will raise `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'`. Second, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (lines 838-843 of `paginator.py`) implements `get_item_key` using `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)` and `value_from_cursor` by returning the raw numeric cursor value, rather than converting `datetime` objects to/from timestamps like `DateTimePaginator` does; ordering by `-datetime` will therefore fail with `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` when building cursors (and pass a numeric cursor value against a `datetime` column on subsequent requests). Finally, these audit-log and paginator changes are completely unrelated to the PR's stated purpose of optimizing spans buffer insertion.

findings.title: Allowing negative cursor offsets in `BasePaginator` and `OptimizedCursorPaginator` causes `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported` in Django QuerySets
findings.body: In `BasePaginator.get_result` (line 182) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 877-886), negative `cursor.offset` values are passed directly as the slice start to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (when `cursor.is_prev` is True in `BasePaginator`, or when `enable_advanced_features` is True in `OptimizedCursorPaginator`). Django `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly forbids negative slice indices and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` (or `AssertionError` in older Django versions). In addition, if `start_offset` is negative enough that `stop = start_offset + limit + extra` is also negative or less than `start_offset`, slicing fails before reaching the database. Because `Cursor.from_string` parses user-supplied cursor strings and allows negative integers for `offset`, any client supplying a cursor like `0:-1:1` will trigger an unhandled 500 error on endpoints using `BasePaginator` subclasses.

findings.title: Changing `span-buf:s:*` from Redis sets to sorted sets without migrating or namespacing keys will cause `WRONGTYPE` errors on deploy
findings.body: `process_spans` now writes to `span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:{parent_span_id}` using `ZADD` (line 197), `add-buffer.lua` uses `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE`/`ZPOPMIN`, and `_load_segment_data` reads with `ZSCAN` (line 434), whereas previously these same `span-buf:s:*` keys were Redis `SET`s accessed with `SADD`/`SCARD`/`SUNIONSTORE`/`SSCAN` (with a 1-hour TTL). During a rolling deploy, existing `span-buf:s:*` keys in Redis are still of type `set`, so executing `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, `ZUNIONSTORE`, or `ZSCAN` against them will fail with `redis.exceptions.ResponseError: WRONGTYPE Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value`, crashing consumer batches until old keys expire or are flushed.
